question: Can an explicitly constrained Safe-RADS variant satisfy a preregistered risk and service constraint with a measured bounded efficiency cost?

semantics.hard: deterministic bound; a violating candidate is infeasible and cannot be committed
semantics.chance: probability of violation is at most epsilon under a declared uncertainty model
semantics.risk: expected, quantile, or tail-risk functional used as a measured constraint quantity
semantics.penalty: objective weight that trades cost against risk and cannot establish safety

validation_authority.claim_boundary: Java verifies hard constraints before commit; Python never owns durable correctness

execution_policy.resource_envelope: read-only semantic formalization; zero external writes

limitations: Formal constraint semantics do not establish observed safety or service performance.
A chance constraint requires calibrated uncertainty and observed outcomes before any claim.
Penalty-only variants remain objective tradeoffs and cannot use safety wording.
Efficiency cost is reported separately and cannot offset a violated hard constraint.
Any parameter or metric change requires a new mechanism version and digest.
